title: Security agent run ledger — shard schema
description: Per-run ledger for the nightly security agent (intent #4290). Each stage writes ONE object of this shape under s3://<findings-bucket>/security-agent/runs/<YYYY-MM-DD>/. No stage read-modify-writes a shared object (FR-C29): shards are merged at read time by the renderer. This file is the single source of truth for (a) which fields a stage may write, (b) how each field merges across shards, and (c) which fields may reach the rendered report (NT-11).

schema_version.description: Envelope version. Bump only for breaking shard-shape changes.

run_date.description: The run's YYYY-MM-DD, matching its S3 prefix (FR-C28).

stage.description: Unique writer id within the run. The optional dotted suffix is what makes concurrent writers land on DISTINCT keys: the two architect halves write 'workflow.code-review' and 'workflow.pentest'; operations writes one shard per story, 'ops.<story-number>'. Two writers sharing a stage id would overwrite each other, which is why the id — not the field set — is the concurrency boundary.

stage_type.description: Must equal the part of `stage` before the first dot. Selects the field allow-list.

generated_at.description: When the writing stage produced this shard. Supplied BY THE WRITER, never read from a clock by the renderer — this field is how a timestamp reaches the report without making the renderer impure (NFR-6).

fields.description: Payload. Every key must appear in x-fields with this shard's stage_type in its `stages` list; anything else is rejected at write time (NT-11, write side).

identified_raw.description: Vulnerabilities the stage reported before dedup. Sums because the two concurrent halves each report their own.

new_finding_ids.description: Opaque service finding ids only — never titles, paths or reproduction detail (C-8). Present so coverage can be checked by identity rather than by comparing two counts that can both be wrong.

run_duration_seconds.description: Wall-clock seconds for the stage. Merges with max, not sum: the two halves overlap in time, so summing would over-report the run.

pentest_cost_usd.description: Reported cost of the pentest half (FR-B8).

daily_epic.description: Issue number of that night's dated EPIC. `single`: two different values is a bug, not something to reconcile.

story_ids.description: Issue numbers of the stories filed. Lets reconciliation name WHICH story is unaccounted for instead of only reporting a delta.

findings_covered.description: Finding ids that the filed stories cover. Compared against new_finding_ids for the coverage half of FR-C32.

planned_sequence.description: Story numbers in dependency order (FR-C21). `single` because order carries meaning — merging two orderings would invent a third.

story_status.description: Keyed by story number as a string. One ops shard per story, so map-union never has to resolve a conflict; a genuine conflict (same story, two different records) is raised rather than silently resolved.

reason.description: Required non-null when status is `stuck` (FR-C37). A closed enum rather than free text: this value is rendered into the report, and free text here is the path by which exploit detail reaches a document (NT-11).

failed_runs.description: Failed developer runs on this story. 3 is the stuck threshold (D-19).

last_transition_at.description: Last state change. 24h without one is the other stuck path (D-19).

x-stuck-rule.description: D-19. Either path independently makes a story stuck, with the reason stamped. Without a definition a run never finalizes.
